title: Module Review Quiz: Functions (CPP_152 to CPP_158)

slides.title: Functions Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers function declarations, definitions, return types, pass-by-value vs pass-by-reference, default parameters, function overloading, and recursion (CPP_152 to CPP_158).

slides.title: Function Declaration (CPP_152)
slides.prompt: Fill in the return type used for a function that does NOT return any value.
options: void
int
null
empty

slides.title: Function Prototype (CPP_152)
slides.prompt: Why do we use a function prototype (declaration) before the main() function in C++?
options: To inform the compiler about the function's name, return type, and parameters before its actual implementation
To automatically execute the function during compilation
To make the function run faster
To turn the function into a global variable
slides.correctAnswer: To inform the compiler about the function's name, return type, and parameters before its actual implementation

slides.title: Return Keyword (CPP_153)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to send a result back to the caller from inside a function.
options: return
send
give
output

slides.title: Pass by Value (CPP_154)
slides.prompt: What happens when a variable is passed by value to a function?
options: A copy of the argument is passed, so original variable remains unchanged
The memory address is passed, modifying original variable
The program creates a pointer variable automatically
It results in a compile-time error
slides.correctAnswer: A copy of the argument is passed, so original variable remains unchanged

slides.title: Pass by Reference (CPP_154)
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol used in a parameter list to allow a function to modify the original argument variable.

slides.title: Default Arguments (CPP_155)
slides.prompt: Where must default argument values be specified in function definitions?
options: In the parameter list, typically starting from rightmost parameters
Inside the body of the function only
In the main function before calling
At the very end of the C++ file
slides.correctAnswer: In the parameter list, typically starting from rightmost parameters

slides.title: Default Parameters (CPP_155)
slides.prompt: Fill in the assignment value so 'country' defaults to 'Myanmar' if omitted.

slides.title: Function Overloading (CPP_156)
slides.prompt: What allows two or more functions to share the exact same name in C++?
options: They must have different parameter types or number of parameters
They must have different return types only
They must be placed in different header files
They must use the inline keyword
slides.correctAnswer: They must have different parameter types or number of parameters

slides.title: Overloading Parameters (CPP_156)
slides.prompt: Fill in the parameter type to successfully overload printData for floating numbers.
slides.codeSnippet:
void printData(int x);
void printData(___ x); // Overloaded version
options: double
int
void
const

slides.title: Recursion Concept (CPP_157)
options: A function calling itself directly or indirectly
A loop that executes indefinitely
A function that takes another function as parameter
Converting a function into an inline assembly block
slides.correctAnswer: A function calling itself directly or indirectly

slides.title: Base Case in Recursion (CPP_157)
slides.prompt: Fill in the base condition check to prevent infinite stack calls in recursive factorial calculation.

slides.title: Inline Functions (CPP_158)
slides.prompt: What is the purpose of using the 'inline' keyword before a short function definition?
options: Suggests the compiler substitute function calls with actual code to reduce call overhead
Hides the function from other source files
Forces the function to run asynchronously
Prevents the function from taking any arguments
slides.correctAnswer: Suggests the compiler substitute function calls with actual code to reduce call overhead
